comparator.name: Molecular and Biophysical Life Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official student curriculum states a complete 180-EC structure: 75 EC of mandatory foundation courses, a 15-EC bachelor research project, 45 EC of major-bound electives and 45 EC of free elective space. The programme page names the ten 7.5-EC mandatory courses. Students choose six major-bound electives, at least four at level 3, using four advisory profiles. The generic normalized target names no profile. Genes to Organisms is selected by official order, independently of UCR fit, and reconstructed with two level-2 and four level-3 courses marked for that profile in the official 2026-2027 overview. The free-elective space remains open.
components: Physical Chemistry for the Life Sciences
Genuine free elective space; no courses are invented for UCR convenience.

core: Molecular and cellular biology, biomolecules and the processes that make life possible
Chemistry, pharmaceutical science and molecular explanations of health, disease and medicines
Biological physics, mathematics and quantitative modelling of living systems
Experimental molecular biology, biochemistry, microscopy and laboratory research
Programming, statistics, bioinformatics and analysis of biological data
Genes, organisms, development, immunity and interactions across biological scales
adjacent: Genes to Organisms and Molecules & Cells
Molecules & Medicine, pharmacology, infection and drug innovation
Biophysics & Modeling, computational biology and quantitative life science
questions: How do molecular and cellular processes generate biological function and disease?
How can experiments, imaging and computation reveal the behaviour of cells and biomolecules?
How can molecular life science contribute to medicines and societal challenges?

routeSelection.basis: The generic target does not name one of the four advisory elective profiles, and none is formally broader than the others. The current curriculum lists Genes to Organisms first, so it is selected by official order before UCR course selection. Six linked electives are instantiated while the separate 45-EC free-elective space remains open.

alternatives.label: Molecular, Cellular & Biophysical Life Sciences
alternatives.labelReason: Molecular-cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, immunology, physiology and experimental/data methods form a coherent health-facing biological direction supported by the programme’s cells, genomics, bioinformatics, neurobiology and health interests.
alternatives.concept: The closest feasible UCR response integrates molecular and cellular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, laboratory work, disease mechanisms, pharmacology, mathematics, statistics and biological data.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes dependent molecular, physiological and biomedical study; mathematical and statistical foundations precede advanced quantitative work. Laboratory, cellular and research-method courses develop from foundations to advanced research, with every course in an available semester.

alternatives.label: Molecules, Medicines & Translational Biology
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule follows the comparator's molecules-to-organism biomedical core, disease mechanisms, laboratory and quantitative research, translation and societal impact.
alternatives.concept: A molecules-and-medicine route combining cell biology, biochemistry, genetics, infection, disease mechanisms and pharmacology with physiology, diagnosis, treatment and developmental health.
progression: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine precedes dependent biomedical study; mathematical and statistical foundations precede advanced quantitative work. Laboratory, molecular, physiological and research-method courses develop from introductory to advanced level, and every course is offered in its assigned term.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, five courses replace programming, computer vision, deep learning, machine learning and psycholinguistics with epidemiology, statistics, ethics, health psychology and an advanced research seminar. The resulting programme gives medicines, disease, population health and translational research a clearly stronger organising role.

alternatives.label: Biophysics, Modelling & Biomedical Data
alternatives.concept: A biophysics-and-modelling route strengthening molecular life science with programming, image analysis, databases, machine learning, probability and advanced quantitative research.
alternatives.labelReason: The course set contains a sustained computing, mathematical and data sequence alongside body systems and disease biology.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match, four courses replace neurobiology, anatomy, pharmacology and psycholinguistics with linear algebra, numerical methods, signal systems and probability. Seven courses differ from the molecules-and-medicine route, yielding a materially more mathematical, computational and modelling-centred curriculum.
progression: Life and brain gateway courses precede advanced disease or neuroscience work; introductory programming and mathematics precede computational methods. Laboratory, molecular and quantitative study build toward advanced disease, modelling and data analysis, and every course is offered in its assigned term.

blocks: Both establish foundations in cells, biomolecules, DNA and essential biological processes.
Both study proteins, nucleic acids, metabolism and the chemistry of biological processes.
Both connect genetic regulation and molecular change with development and disease; UCR is broader pathology and genetics.
Both connect molecular and cellular foundations to organismal and physiological function; UCR is human-centred.
Both study neural systems, biological mechanisms and behaviour; UCR provides an introductory rather than advanced molecular treatment.
Both examine immune mechanisms and interactions with pathogenic microorganisms.
Both examine molecular and cellular mechanisms whose disruption affects development and disease; UCR is broader disease mechanisms.
Both examine drug molecules, targets, action and disposition; UCR is pharmacology rather than organic synthesis.
Both develop practical molecular-biology and biochemical laboratory skills.
Both develop statistics and experimental analysis; Utrecht additionally integrates Python and academic writing.
The advanced research seminar develops research design and analysis, but does not reproduce Utrecht’s compulsory 15-EC laboratory thesis.
Both develop mathematics for quantitative life science; UCR does not combine this with programming in the same course.
Both apply contemporary quantitative technologies to biological or health problems; UCR contributes machine learning rather than biotechnology.
UCR has no scheduled course with the dedicated physical-chemistry and spectroscopy scope of this foundation.
UCR has quantitative and biological foundations but no dedicated biological-physics course matching this component.
UCR lacks a dedicated structural-biology and biophysical-methods course with microscopy and spectroscopy practice.
No single selected UCR course reproduces this integrated molecular-to-tissue component.
The 45-EC Utrecht free-elective space remains genuinely open and is not assigned invented UCR counterparts.

selection.assessment: The broad closest match substantively covers the Genes to Organisms and Molecules & Cells directions. Molecules & Medicine and Biophysics & Modeling each generate a coherent, feasible and materially distinct UCR route. Their schedules differ pairwise by four to ten courses and pass all hard constraints, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

notes.text: Both programmes support substantial molecular, cellular, biomedical, quantitative and laboratory study. Utrecht additionally requires physical chemistry, biological physics, structural-biology methods, six major-bound electives and a 15-EC laboratory thesis. UCR can combine life science, biomedicine, data science and mathematics, but does not reproduce that full specialist chemistry/biophysics sequence or compulsory laboratory capstone.
